nodes.label: Boat Rules
nodes.rationale: Any player may move an empty boat freely. One boat per sea space. Each boat carries at most 3 people (any colors). Control of a loaded boat: the player with the most pieces on it; ties mean both control it. Moving a loaded boat into a sea serpent space removes boat and passengers; into a whale space removes the boat and passengers become swimmers (removed too if a shark is there).

nodes.label: Game Components
nodes.rationale: 1 board, 40 land tiles (16 beach, 16 forest, 8 mountain), 40 people (10 in each of 4 colors), 5 sea serpents, 6 sharks, 5 whales, 4 dolphins (optional rule 5 only), 12 boats, 1 red creature die, 2 blue dive dice (optional rule 5 only), 1 tile bag, 1 rulebook. Each person has a hidden number 1-6 underneath = its score if rescued. 2-4 players.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Roll Creature Die
nodes.rationale: Roll the red creature die, then you MAY move one creature of the rolled type (if any on the board), either to attack others or protect your own people.

nodes.label: Defensive Tiles
nodes.rationale: Repel shark: when an opponent moves a shark onto a space with your swimmer, play to remove the shark before it eats your swimmer. Repel whale: when an opponent moves a whale onto a space with a boat you control, play to remove the whale and keep the boat safe. Played only on another player's turn in reaction to a creature move.

nodes.label: Goal: Highest Sum of Saved People
nodes.norm_label: goal: highest sum of saved people
nodes.rationale: Before the volcano tile is revealed, rescue as many people as possible. The winner is the player whose SUM of saved people's numbers is highest (not necessarily the most pieces).

nodes.label: Phase 2: Move People & Boats
nodes.rationale: Up to 3 moves total (3 land or sea spaces) split between your people and boats. Goal: board people onto boats and carry them to safe islands.

nodes.label: Safe Island Arrival
nodes.rationale: People disembark from a boat in one of the two sea spaces adjacent to a safe island; each disembarkation costs one move. A swimmer moving from an adjacent sea space to a safe island also costs one move. Rescued pieces are never moved again.

nodes.label: End Game & Scoring
nodes.rationale: When the volcano tile is revealed, the volcano destroys the rest of Atlantis and people still en route, and the game ends. A player with no pieces to move skips phase 2 but the game continues. At the end, all rescued pieces are returned and their numbers summed; the highest total wins, not the most pieces.

nodes.label: Setup Procedure
nodes.rationale: Ordered setup: place 5 sea serpents on marked sea spaces; shuffle land tiles face-up onto black-edged sea spaces to build the island; each player takes a color and 10 people; 2 boats each; remaining sharks/whales/boats set aside; first player random or agreed; players secretly view their own numbers; place people one per empty tile in clockwise order until all 10 placed; then place boats one per empty sea space adjacent to a land tile. After the game starts you may never look at or show your numbers again.

nodes.label: Swimmer Rules
nodes.rationale: A piece becomes a swimmer by moving from an adjacent tile to sea, diving from a boat, falling into the sea when its tile is removed, or when its boat is capsized by a whale. Each swimmer moves one sea space per turn; can board a boat only in the same sea space; multiple swimmers may share a space; moving into a space with a sea serpent or shark removes the swimmer immediately.

nodes.label: Tile Categories
nodes.rationale: Three categories: 'play immediately' (shark, whale, boat, whirlpool - revealed and removed), 'play at start of turn' (dolphin, favorable wind, move sea serpent, move shark, move whale - kept face-down in hand), and 'defensive / out of turn' (repel shark, repel whale). Small symbols under tiles are reminders only.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Play Hand Tile
nodes.rationale: Play at most one tile from hand per turn. Skip on the first turn or when holding no tiles.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Remove Land Tile
nodes.rationale: Must remove one tile from the island; people on it become swimmers on that sea space. Look underneath secretly and act per tile rules. Tile choice priorities: must be adjacent to at least one sea space; beaches first, then forests, then mountains; a beach fully enclosed by forest/mountain is removed last.

nodes.label: Four-Phase Turn Structure
nodes.rationale: Each player in clockwise order performs four phases: (1) play a hand tile, (2) move people and boats, (3) remove a land tile, (4) roll the creature die and move a creature.

nodes.label: Volcano Tile
nodes.rationale: One of the mountain tiles has the volcano underneath. As soon as it is revealed, the game ends.

nodes.label: Board SVG (#bd)
nodes.rationale: SVG board element #bd with viewBox 0 0 750 580, inside #bw board wrapper; layered with #die overlay for dice animation.

nodes.label: Bundled Game JavaScript
nodes.rationale: The esbuild bundle of src/*.ts inlined into the page script, replacing the /*BUNDLE*/ placeholder.

nodes.label: Engine Constants (CONT, W, H, SAFE, DIE...)
nodes.norm_label: engine constants (cont, w, h, safe, die...)
nodes.rationale: Bundled engine data: CONT tile counts (shark 6, whale 5, boat 4, whirl 2, volc 1, dolph 3, wind 3, mserp 2, mshark 2, mwhale 2, rshark 5, rwhale 5), board W=17 H=11, SAFE islands at corners, DOCK mapping, SERP start spaces, CUT spaces, NUMS [1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,5,6], MV/RANGE creature movement, DIE faces (serp,serp,shark,shark,whale,whale), PUBLIC tile list.

nodes.label: RTL Persian Theme & Dark Mode
nodes.rationale: lang=fa dir=rtl, Vazirmatn font, CSS variables with light/dark themes (prefers-color-scheme and data-theme override), safe-area insets, overscroll-behavior none, prefers-reduced-motion support.

nodes.label: Zoom Controls (#zc)
nodes.rationale: Floating control cluster bottom-left: zoom in (＋), zoom out (－), fit (⤢), and sound toggle (🔊) buttons, 40px round touch targets.

nodes.label: Dockerfile Deployment
nodes.rationale: Any host running Node or Docker works (Render, Railway, Fly.io, a VPS). Start command npm start; port read from PORT env var; client auto-selects wss:// when the host provides HTTPS.

nodes.label: src/engine.ts Game Rules Module
nodes.rationale: Game rules; no DOM and no I/O (runs in both browser and Node), fully typed.

nodes.label: Escape from Atlantis Online Game
nodes.rationale: Digital implementation of the board game Survive: Escape from Atlantis for 2-4 players, with local (single screen, turn-based) and online (each player on own device) modes.

nodes.label: Current Limitations
nodes.rationale: Single server instance (room state in memory, saved to a file; multi-server needs shared storage like Redis). No login/accounts; anyone knowing the room code can join before start. Rooms idle 24h are cleaned. Optional rules not yet implemented.

nodes.label: data/rooms.json Room Persistence
nodes.rationale: DATA_FILE env var changes the room save path (default data/rooms.json). On hosts with ephemeral disks, attach persistent storage so games survive restarts.

nodes.label: server.ts Room Server
nodes.rationale: Server: rooms, seats, reconnection, per-player views.

nodes.label: Test Suite
nodes.rationale: engine-test.ts: 45 precise rule tests plus 200 random in-engine games. server-test.ts: input sanitization and room code structure. fuzz.ts: 300 full random games (must all finish without errors or tile-content leaks). online-test.ts: real server + 3 WebSocket clients, full networked game, mid-game disconnect/reconnect, secrets never reaching others. ui-smoke.ts: quick DOM-stub check of the built output without a browser.

nodes.label: src/ui.ts UI Module
nodes.rationale: Interface: display and clicks only; handles both local and online modes.

nodes.label: WebSocket Protocol
nodes.rationale: Client to server: {type:'create',n,name}, {type:'join',code,name}, {type:'rejoin',code,token}, {type:'action',a}. Server to client: joined{code,seat,token}, lobby{code,n,names}, state{view,events,names,connected}, error{msg}.

nodes.label: /*BUNDLE*/ Placeholder
nodes.rationale: Marker inside the script tag of shell.html that the build replaces with the bundled game JavaScript.

nodes.label: Shell Layout Structure
nodes.rationale: Layout: #app column with #main (player chips #sc, board #bw with #bd svg, #die overlay, zoom controls #zc) and #side (status bar #bar with step header #stph, status #st, hand #hand, card detail #cd, buttons #bt; collapsible log #lgd). Overlay #ov for modals. Landscape media query moves #side beside the board.

nodes.label: Survive: Escape from Atlantis Rules
nodes.rationale: Rewritten summary in own words of the official Stronghold Games rules. Source: UltraBoardGames base rules and optional rules pages. Check exact tile symbols and board dimensions in your own edition booklet.

nodes.label: Built index.html (Shell + Bundle)
nodes.rationale: Built output: shell + bundle, a single self-contained file. Contains the full CSS/HTML layout plus the bundled game JavaScript (engine, UI, graphics, sound).

nodes.label: Shell HTML Template
nodes.rationale: Page template (CSS) with a /*BUNDLE*/ placeholder where the esbuild bundle is injected to produce public/index.html.

nodes.label: esbuild + tsc Build Pipeline
nodes.rationale: npm run build bundles the whole app with esbuild into a single self-contained file (public/index.html) and builds server and tests with tsc into dist/. shell.html is the page template with a /*BUNDLE*/ placeholder.

nodes.label: Hidden Information Protection
nodes.rationale: Hidden info (tile contents on the board, opponents' piece numbers, opponents' hand tiles) never reaches other clients. Only the player who reveals a tile receives the reveal event. The defense window is shown to all involved players whether or not they hold a tile, so nobody can guess who has one.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Layout
nodes.rationale: Thumb-friendly: status bar and buttons at the bottom, compact player score row on top, collapsible game log. Board pans with one finger, zooms with pinch or +/- buttons, ⤢ refits. In landscape the control panel moves beside the board. Touch targets at least 44px.

nodes.label: Reconnect via localStorage Token
nodes.rationale: Each player has a token stored in browser localStorage. If the page closes or the internet drops, they return to the same seat via 'continue previous game' or automatically.

nodes.label: Server as Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Game state lives only on the server. Client sends an action like {t:'movePerson',p:3,to:'7,5'}; the server validates and executes it via engine.apply and sends each player their own engine.view. Dice are rolled only by the server using a seed stored in state.

nodes.label: SVG Vector Graphics
nodes.rationale: All pieces are vector SVG drawings, not emoji: people (player-colored), sailboat, sea serpent, shark, whale, safe island, anchor. They render identically on every device. Code lives in src/gfx.ts.

nodes.label: WebAudio Procedural Sound
nodes.rationale: Sound is synthesized with WebAudio in src/sfx.ts (no audio files). The 🔊 button next to zoom toggles it and the choice is remembered in the browser. Infinite animations are disabled when the device has reduced-motion enabled.
